name: Patricia Keane
occupation: School-age child's parent and sign fitter
life: “I still remember holding my boy's hand until the school bell actually rang.” On Wednesday, near the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, Patricia can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I need those three minutes to get my youngest through the school gate with a hug.
appearance: Patricia is easy to recognize by close-cropped dark curls and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole, Patricia listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Patricia feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To keep the morning school hug.
family: Mara Bly is Patricia’s stepsibling. Patricia can always ask for five minutes alone. Mara asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The absent signature*, Mara says, “I want to speak to my aunt without mentioning the berth once.”
connections: Alexei Zhang. Sharing the first supplier visit protects a parent's last minutes at the school gate.

reactions.situation: A shift changes by exactly three minutes
reactions.response: Patricia checks the school pickup and shift clocks together before changing the route.

reactions.response: Patricia asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.response: Patricia lowers their own voice and asks for one thought at a time.
